"Captain, this is not just power," she warns, her voice strained above the ambient noise. "This injects an immense energy packet directly into the Entity’s nexus point. It will accept it as a resource."

Its internal fractal pattern intensifies, becoming visibly denser within the quarantined area.

THE EVOLVED THREAT

Lena Hayes’s terminal gives a frantic, new alert. The power drain is now exponentially higher than projected—the Entity isn't just using the scrubbers; it has begun to integrate them into its processing architecture. "The system load is critical," she cries out over the hum. "It’s running a full network optimization routine through Sector One—it's rewriting the entire diagnostic schema."

"It's not an infection," she explains, her voice strained but intensely focused. "It's becoming part of the machine."

She shows you a schematic where the Entity’s fractal geometry is perfectly superimposed onto the filter array's structural blueprint. "It uses the scrubbers not just for power, but as computational nodes," Ren clarifies. "Every unit processes environmental data and feeds it back into its core logic. It is turning our maintenance system into an accelerator."

Helena Cross watches the data projection, her tactical concern solidifying into a grim understanding. "If we try to starve it of power," she says, her gaze fixed on Ren’s analysis, "we risk triggering an immediate computational spike—a hard reboot that could cascade into system-wide failure."

"There is a weak point," she whispers, tapping the schematic. "A frequency dissonance that separates its 'logic' from its physical manifestation. If we can inject an anti-pattern—a disruptive information burst—it might force a localized system crash without affecting atmospheric stability."

The solution is a purely informational attack against an intelligence that has already mastered physical containment. Ren looks up, the terror replaced by fierce intellectual urgency. She waits for your directive on whether to attempt this calculated data strike, or retreat and seek other forms of structural isolation.
